lessons.title: What Connect actually depends on
lessons.why: You cannot debug a contact center if you treat AWS as a logo on the invoice.
paras: Amazon Connect, called Amazon Connect Customer in the admin guide after the 28 April 2026 family announcement, is a multi-tenant contact center in a Region you choose. The instance does not contain IAM, S3, Lambda, Kinesis, or CloudWatch. It calls them.
This campus starts here because every later fault lands in one of those services: a key policy, a log group, a stream shard, a Regional endpoint, or a firewall.
points: The family name Amazon Connect now covers Customer, Health, Decisions, and Talent. This campus teaches the contact center.
IAM prefixes you will meet include connect, profile, cases, wisdom, and voiceid. voiceid is historical after 20 May 2026.
The data plane for agents is the browser, not a PBX firmware image.
Shared responsibility: AWS runs the platform. You run flows, identity, keys, numbers, quotas, and the agent network.
lessons.mistake: Starting in the flow designer before you can name the Region and the account.

flow.label: Region
flow.detail: The instance does not move by itself.

lessons.title: Regions, endpoints, and why Osaka is special
lessons.why: A Region is a capacity, latency, and residency boundary. It is not a checkbox you can flip on a live number.
paras: The instance, its numbers, and its logs are Regional. Global Resiliency is the only supported way to link two instances, and only in published pairs: Northern Virginia with Oregon, Frankfurt with London, Tokyo with Osaka.
Osaka is a replica Region for Tokyo. Numbers have to be enabled for Global Resiliency, and delivery through Osaka can take up to 20 seconds. That is a design input, not a footnote.
points: New accounts start at two instances per Region.
Quota raises are per Region. Raising Oregon does not raise Virginia.
The CCP domain is instance.my.connect.aws. The old awsapps.com domain is documented as going away.
Softphone TURN endpoints are Regional. A laptop in another country still talks to the instance Region.
lessons.mistake: Putting the 'second Region' in a city that is not in a supported pair and calling it resiliency.

lessons.title: IAM is not the security profile
lessons.why: Agents get a security profile. Automations get an IAM principal. Mixing the names produces a policy that cannot place a call and a user who can.
paras: A security profile decides which buttons a user sees in the admin site and the CCP. An IAM policy decides which AWS API calls a role may make. Connect also relies on resource policies, especially lambda:InvokeFunction for principal connect.amazonaws.com.
The service-linked role is what Connect uses to write recordings and logs. A customer-managed KMS key still needs a key policy that trusts that role, or the put succeeds in your mind and fails in S3.
points: connect:StartOutboundVoiceContact and StartChatContact are privileged. Do not put them on a public web role.
profile and cases are separate IAM services.
wisdom is still the prefix you will see for agent assist in the service authorization reference.
Least privilege means the instance ARN, not Resource star, once the design is real.
lessons.mistake: Granting an agent AdministratorAccess because the security profile looked empty.

lessons.title: Lambda is a seam, not a place to hide a CRM
lessons.why: The flow will not wait for a slow system of record. Design the function for the timeout you actually have.
paras: Synchronous invoke waits at most 8 seconds. Asynchronous mode can be paired with a Wait of up to 60 seconds. A chain of Lambda calls in one contact must stay within 20 seconds.
Connect retries throttles and HTTP 500s, up to three times, until the block timeout. Your function should be safe to run twice.
points: Add the function to the instance. An identity policy alone does not let the flow invoke it.
Return a flat string map or JSON, matching the block. Nested objects fail a string-map block.
Log the ContactId. The flow log has no Lambda RequestId to join on.
Default block timeout is 3 seconds. Raise it on purpose, not by hoping.
lessons.mistake: Setting the Lambda console timeout to 30 seconds and assuming the flow will wait.

lessons.title: S3 holds the proof
lessons.why: Recordings, chat transcripts, exported reports, and attachments are objects. If the bucket policy is wrong, the contact still 'succeeds' and the file is missing.
paras: You choose the bucket and the optional customer-managed key when you configure storage. The service-linked role writes the objects. Lifecycle rules are yours: a regulator's retention period is not an AWS default.
A third-party quality tool usually reads the same object after the CTR arrives and names the key. Design the prefix so a ContactId finds one recording.
points: Block public access. These objects are conversations.
KMS and the bucket policy are both required when you use a customer-managed key.
Attachment size defaults to 20 MB and can be set up to 100 MB.
Email has its own storage path through the email channel and Amazon SES networking guidance.
lessons.mistake: Turning on recording in the flow and never checking that an object landed.

lessons.title: Kinesis is how the ecosystem listens
lessons.why: Anything that must react to agents or to finished contacts needs a stream, not a person refreshing a report.
paras: Agent events and contact trace records can go to Kinesis Data Streams or Firehose. Streams let several consumers read. Firehose is the buffered path to S3. One quiet five-minute stretch is the documented moment to look at delivery errors.
A single shard is a common starting size for agent events and a common cause of lag once WFM and a custom dashboard both read it.
points: CTRs are near real time, not instant, and consumers must tolerate duplicates.
Only one Firehose is the default CTR delivery. Fan out by consuming a stream.
Join on ContactId. There is no other honest key.
Agent events are the adherence feed. Historical reports are not.
lessons.mistake: Pointing two WFM products at one shard and discovering lag during a Monday peak.

lessons.title: CloudWatch tells you the flow ran
lessons.why: Without flow logs you are guessing which block took the error branch.
paras: Set logging behavior writes a record per block to CloudWatch Logs. Search for Results like Error, and filter the Lambda block type InvokeExternalResource. The ContactId is the join to Lambda's own log if the function printed it.
The email quota note recommends an alarm at 80 percent of concurrent emails. Use the same habit for calls, chats, and tasks.
points: Logging can be turned off in the flow. Check that before you blame the log group.
A missing error in Lambda's log with an error in the flow log means Connect rejected the response before or without a completed invoke.
Metrics such as ConcurrentEmails belong in an alarm, not in a monthly slide.
Flow logs are not a recording and not a CTR.
lessons.mistake: Editing the flow again before you have read the log of the failed ContactId.

lessons.title: The network path is part of the product
lessons.why: Connect's softphone is WebRTC in the agent's browser. A firewall designed for a desk phone will block it.
paras: Option 1 is a domain allow list: the instance on TCP 443, telemetry, transport, and TurnNlb on UDP 3478. Option 2 is the AWS IP ranges and is documented as not recommended. Test more than 200 calls. An error rate above 2 percent points at proxy or DNS resolution.
Media should not hairpin through a VPN. Stateless firewalls also need the browser's ephemeral UDP range, because there is no lasting 'pin' the way people imagine.
points: The usual failure string names turn:TurnNlb and port 3478.
ice_collection_timeout means the browser never gathered candidates.
A custom CCP can be media-less, but then you still do not have a softphone.
Video adds a Chime subnet and does not support VDI.
lessons.mistake: Opening TCP 443 and declaring the softphone done.

lessons.title: Certifications and the badges that are not certifications
lessons.why: There is no Amazon Connect specialty exam on the AWS Certification catalog. Pretending a badge is that exam misleads a hiring plan.
paras: The catalog's foundational exams are AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner and AWS Certified AI Practitioner. The associate exam that best covers the surrounding design is AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate. Developer - Associate fits Lambda and Streams. CloudOps Engineer - Associate fits quotas and operations. Security - Specialty fits IAM and KMS.

AWS Certified Advanced Networking - Specialty is the exam for complex networks, and its last day is 31 December 2026. Connect-specific recognition is a set of Skill Builder learning plans with Credly badges, passed at 80 percent: Communications Specialist, Fundamentals, AI Fundamentals, and Developer, plus an administrator track.
points: Cloud Practitioner is the shared vocabulary of accounts, Regions, and billing.
AI Practitioner is context for generative features. It does not configure a flow.
The Communications Specialist badge covers telephony, IVR, flows, routing, and omnichannel.
A badge is issued through Credly within about two weeks of the knowledge check. It is not a proctored certification.
lessons.mistake: Listing 'Connect certified' on a design document because someone finished a free knowledge check.

lessons.title: A depends-on map you can defend
lessons.why: Every later track names the foundation it needs. If that foundation is missing, the track's lab will show the same fault.
paras: Telephony depends on the instance and on quotas. Flows depend on telephony only because a number has to enter somewhere. Lambda depends on IAM. The CCP depends on the network lesson. Analytics depends on Kinesis and S3. Global Resiliency depends on identity, numbers, and a supported Region pair.
The Ecosystem track depends on all of those, because WFM, quality, E911, and the CRM are consumers of ContactId, recordings, agent events, and profiles.
points: Read the depends-on line on each track before you skip ahead.
A migration bridge without flows and routing is a glossary, not a plan.
E911 depends on Profiles, Lambda, and an outbound whisper flow.
Price estimates depend on the rate card date, which this campus stamps as 14 October 2026.

lessons.title: Feature timeline
lessons.why: Names moved. Features mostly stayed. Voice ID did not.
paras: The timeline in this campus is a study map. Dates come from AWS What's New, the admin guide, the AWS News Blog, or a compiled timeline that cites those pages and was checked on 25 September 2026. Where the admin guide applies the 2026 product name to a 2017 row, the timeline keeps the name used on the day.
Read it before you use an old runbook. Contact Lens means conversational analytics. Amazon Q in Connect means agent assist. High-volume outbound means campaigns. Voice ID means ended.
points: 2020-07-23, Contact Lens generally available.
2026-04-28, the family announcement.
2026-05-20, Voice ID end of support.
lessons.mistake: Quoting a document-history row's 2026 wording as if that was the 2017 name.
